title: Colours
label: ch:colours
canDo: I can name four basic colours in French, put a colour after the noun it describes, and say which of them are not Latin.

payoff.summary: Four colours with two different homelands. noir walked down from Latin niger and rouge from a root older than Latin — the same one behind English red, rust and German rot. But blanc and bleu are Frankish, Germanic words that displaced Latin ones inside a Romance language, which is the opposite of the usual traffic. albus did not die when blanc took its job; it stopped being a colour and became l'aube, the dawn. And the colour goes after its noun — le vin rouge — with bonjour as the exception the reader already says every day.
payoff.note: Authored when chapter 16 left the hand-written set: two schema-v1 lessons held four colours, and the .tex taught adjective POSITION (le vin rouge) inside a grammarlens that no lesson owned. Eight lessons now own one thing each. The payoff is atom-scored -- it assesses every knowledge atom its chapter introduces; the chapter's one culture claim is assessed by FR-C13-tricolore.
